page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8ae.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 4 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, running at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. It features 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 instruction/data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, and network connectivity is limited to a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 3112.08 and Geekbench single-core reaching 2007.0, both placing in the top 25%. Text processing performance is also strong at 2521.0. However, multi-core and parallel workloads show average to weak results. The Geekbench multi-core score of 4496.0 and stress-ng multi-core score of 6229.69 fall into the middle 50%, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (26.67 GB/sec) and software compilation with Clang (5418.0) are in the bottom 25%. Database operations and Redis SET operations (5.66 million operations/sec) also perform in the lower tier.

Given its high memory density relative to compute resources, the ecs.r8ae.xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive multi-threaded processing or local storage. The absence of local NVMe drives and the baseline 4 Gbps network limit its suitability for high-throughput storage systems or heavy web serving. It is best suited for memory-intensive applications, caching layers, lightweight database hosting, and text processing tasks that benefit from dedicated CPU cores and a high RAM-to-vCPU ratio.
